title: Japan, Dec 2026 · 8 friends
brief:
# Trip brief

I will be in Tokyo 15–19 Dec, Hakone 19–21, Osaka 21–26 (Osaka base, but during the day we will
commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed, ending the night/nightlife in Osaka; if there are cool nightlife
things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them), then Tokyo again 26–29 Dec 2026.

We land at Haneda Terminal 3 on Tue 15 Dec around 15:00 and fly home from Haneda Terminal 3 on
Tue 29 Dec at 17:20.

We are a group of 8, all around 20 years old, all Asian. We love to drink, and we want to maximise
all the time we've got in the country. Think about things like Round1, shopping, and so on; we love
to do it all. No go-karts. Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes.

Stays (already booked): Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara,
Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo).

stays.name: Ninja House (Airbnb) — Toshima
stays.notes: Ninja House｜2 bathrooms｜near Ikebukuro｜10 guests. Host: Yoko. Keypad self check-in. 9 min walk from Ochiai-minami-nagasaki (Toei Ōedo line) — direct to Shinjuku, Roppongi, Tsukijishijo, Ueno-okachimachi. Free cancellation before Nov 15 4PM.

stays.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa (Airbnb) — Sengokuhara
stays.notes: Hot Spring Hakone Villa, Easy Access, Piano. Host: Eika. Lockbox self check-in. Access guide was sent in Airbnb messages. Private onsen. Free cancellation before Dec 14 3PM.

stays.name: Kujō House (Airbnb) — Nishi-ku, Osaka
stays.notes: (ちよ)桜と過ごすお部屋 — 4 bedrooms, 2 baths, 4 toilets. Host: Tatsu. Lockbox. Kujō stn (Chūō line + Hanshin Namba line): Namba 6 min, direct trains to Kintetsu-Nara & Kobe-Sannomiya. JR Nishikujō → USJ 10 min. Free cancellation before Nov 21 4PM.

stays.name: Garfield House (Airbnb) — Shinjuku 6-chōme
stays.notes: Garfield home whole build — 10 min walk to Shinjuku-sanchōme. Host: Bibo. Lockbox. Max 8 guests. Walk to Golden Gai / Kabukichō / Ni-chōme. Free cancellation before Nov 26 4PM.

days.title: Romancecar out of Tokyo · private onsen soak · Yumoto souvenirs · crystal lights · sushi · geisha drinking games · MONTA till midnight

notes.text: Three things must be booked ahead: Romancecar seats as soon as they open a month out, the Yuryo private baths (they close at 15:00 the day before), and Hakone Sushi plus MONTA by phone. Pre-book every taxi leg as 2 cars.
The 3-day Hakone Freepass at ¥7,500 from Shinjuku covers trains, buses, the ropeway and the pirate ship through Monday. Buy it on EMot before the 19th. The Romancecar seat is extra.
Yumoto shops close around 18:00 and A Coop closes at 18:00. Do all souvenir and booze shopping in the afternoon, because tonight you're only passing back through after dark.
Tonight is the only night that works: Furatto Geisha runs on the 3rd Saturday and MONTA is closed Sunday and Monday. Don't let anything slip.

stops.name: Leave Ninja House (Toshima)
stops.summary: A pre-dawn checkout from Ninja House to start the biggest day of the Hakone leg.
stops.plan: Check out early and head for Shinjuku. If big suitcases were sent ahead to Osaka, travel with day bags only.
stops.transport: JR Yamanote line Ikebukuro → Shinjuku, 9 min, then walk to the Odakyu Romancecar platforms

guide.story: It's dark, cold and quiet in Toshima, and this is the one morning you can't hit snooze. Ikebukuro to Shinjuku on the Yamanote is a short hop, and the hard part is getting all 8 of you out the door at once. If the big suitcases have already been forwarded to Osaka, today is gloriously light: day bags, a change of clothes and phones charged for the Freepass e-tickets.
how: Do a full room sweep the night before so checkout at 06:40 is just grab-and-go.
Take the JR Yamanote line from Ikebukuro to Shinjuku, then follow the signs to the Odakyu line and the Romancecar platforms.
Hit a konbini near Shinjuku for breakfast and drinks to eat on the train.
tips: Put one person in charge of the group chat headcount. Missing a reserved Romancecar seat is the most expensive mistake you can make today.
Open the EMot app and load everyone's tickets before you leave, not on the platform.
wishes: w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
w11: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)

stops.name: Odakyu Romancecar Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto (start of the 3-day Hakone Freepass)
stops.summary: Ride the Romancecar into the mountains, with the Freepass that pays for your whole Hakone weekend.
stops.plan: Sit in your 8 reserved seats with the EMot Freepass e-tickets on your phones. The pass covers the base fare; the Romancecar seat is a separate ticket. Konbini breakfast on board.

guide.story: The Romancecar is Tokyo's weekend escape train. The city thins into rice fields and then forested hills, and you roll into Hakone-Yumoto ready to soak. Your 3-day Freepass starts today and covers the Tozan train, cable car, ropeway, pirate ship and the Sengokuhara buses, plus discounts at around 70 sights. The Romancecar seat is a separate ticket on top of the pass, so the 8 seats together are the thing you lock in early.
how: Buy the 3-day Freepass on Odakyu EMot as a digital ticket (¥7,500 from Shinjuku) and keep it on your phone.
Reserve the Romancecar seats the moment sales open, one month before. Saturday seats in December sell out.
Board, find your 8 seats, and eat your konbini breakfast as the scenery turns green.
tips: Ticket machines only sell same-day passes. Buy online and you skip the counter queue at Shinjuku.
The Odakyu stretch to Odawara is good for one round trip only, so the return to Tokyo uses that up.
Regular sightseeing buses are not covered by the pass, so check the bus livery before you hop on.
guide.booking: Freepass from one month before via EMot; Romancecar seats as soon as they open
wishes: w10: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes
w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Hakone-Yumoto Station – sort bags
stops.summary: Go hands-free at Yumoto so the rest of the day is all fun and no hauling.
stops.plan: Hand big bags to the Hakone Carry Service if the villa accepts deliveries (see todo), or use lockers, so the group travels hands-free until check-in.
stops.transport: Free Hakone Yuryo shuttle from Yumoto Station, every 10–20 min, about 5 min

guide.story: Hakone-Yumoto is the gateway town, a steep, steamy valley of souvenir shops wedged between a river and the hills. Nothing kills the onsen mood like dragging a rolling bag over cobbles, so deal with luggage right here. The Hakone Carry Service can send bags up to the villa if it accepts deliveries. If it doesn't, lockers at the station do the job until you come back through.
how: Check with the villa beforehand whether it accepts Carry Service deliveries.
If it does, drop the bags at the Carry Service counter at the station. If not, split everything across the station lockers.
Pick up the free Hakone Yuryo shuttle from outside the station, or walk it in 18 minutes.
tips: Remember which lockers you used. You're collecting the bags before the taxis this afternoon.
Keep swimwear-free onsen essentials in your day bag: a hair tie, a change of underwear and moisturiser.
wishes: w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Hakone Yuryo – 2 private open-air baths
stops.summary: Two private open-air baths for 2 hours, just your crew, with no strangers.
stops.plan: Two large private open-air rooms from 10:00 to 12:00, so the group soaks together without strangers. Tattoos are OK. Then a beer in the lounge.
stops.address: 神奈川県足柄下郡箱根町塔之澤４
stops.transport: Yuryo shuttle back to Yumoto Station, 13 min, then walk 5 min to the Yaei bridge

guide.story: Hakone Yuryo is a forested day-spa with a big public bath. The real prize is the private open-air rooms: your own stone tub, steam curling into cold December air and the sound of the trees. Two large rooms means you can split boys and girls, or mix however you like, and nobody else walks in. It's been tattoo-OK since 2025, and after the soak there's sake and irori-grill food in the lounge.
how: Book 2 large private rooms for 10:00–12:00. Booking opens one month before and closes at 15:00 the day before.
Arrive right at the 10:00 opening so the full 120 minutes are yours.
Afterwards, meet up in the lounge for a beer and stay until 12:15.
tips: Skip the main bath. Reviews say it gets crowded, and you've paid for the good stuff.
The weekend rate applies, which is ¥10,400 per room. Splitting it 8 ways is a steal for a private onsen.
Drink water between soaks if you're starting on beer before noon.
guide.booking: Private rooms: from one month before until 15:00 the day before

w8: We love to do it all

stops.name: Hatsuhana Soba (Shinkan)
stops.summary: Yumoto's classic soba house on the river bridge: fast, cheap and famous for its yam-tororo.
stops.plan: The classic yam-tororo soba (貞女そば ¥1,000) or tempura soba (¥1,300). Quick and cheap.
stops.address: 635-635 Yumoto, 箱根町 Hakone, Ashigarashimo District, Kanagawa 250-0311
stops.transport: Walk 5 min to the station street

guide.story: Hatsuhana is the soba shop everyone in Yumoto points to. The new building sits right by the Yaei bridge, so you look over the river while you slurp. The house signature is teijo soba, cold noodles under a fluffy mountain of grated yam and egg. It sounds strange and tastes silky. It's a no-booking, in-and-out lunch that leaves time and money for the shopping street.
how: Walk to the Shinkan (new building) by the Yaei bridge after the shuttle back.
Order the 貞女そば (¥1,000), the tempura soba (¥1,300) or plain せいろそば (¥1,200).
Eat and go: the souvenir street is a 5-minute walk.
tips: Groups of 8 may get split across tables for a short wait. Accept it, because it moves.
Point at 貞女そば on the menu if the name is hard to say. It's the one regulars order.
wishes: w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Hakone-Yumoto station shopping street
stops.summary: Hakone's one real souvenir strip, so shop it now while it's open.
stops.plan: Souvenir run: onsen manju, yosegi boxes, fish cakes, local sake. Buy now, because shops close around 18:00 and you'll be back after dark.
stops.transport: Pre-booked taxis (2 cars, collect any stored bags) Yumoto → A Coop Sengokuhara, 23 min. The train-and-bus route takes over 2 hours here.

guide.story: The street climbing from Yumoto Station is a crush of tiny shops: steaming onsen manju, intricate yosegi marquetry puzzle boxes, fish-cake stalls and local sake. It's touristy, but in the good, snack-in-every-hand way. Everything shuts early, around 18:00, and you'll only pass back through in the dark tonight, so this hour is your only shot.
how: Work up one side of the street and back down the other. Grab a fresh manju early to fuel the shopping.
Buy the yosegi boxes and sake here, since they're the real Hakone souvenirs.
Collect any stored bags, then meet the 2 pre-booked taxis for the 23-minute ride to Sengokuhara.
tips: Don't try the train and bus up. Door to door it's 138 minutes, against 23 by taxi.
Fish cakes keep fine until the villa fridge, so they make a good snack for the second night.
Expect slow traffic through the street. Book the taxi pickup at the station end.
wishes: w7: Shopping
w8: We love to do it all

facts.text: Most shops in the shopping street close around 18:00 (shop hours vary by store).

stops.name: A Coop Sengokuhara – villa drinks run
stops.summary: The booze run that fuels two onsen nights at the villa.
stops.plan: Stock up on beer, chu-hi, sake and snacks for two onsen nights, plus breakfast for Sun and Mon. It closes at 18:00, so this is the only chance.
stops.transport: Taxi (2 cars) to the villa, 6 min

guide.story: A Coop is Sengokuhara's local supermarket, the place where big villa groups load trolleys with cans before vanishing into the hills. Up here the shops close early and there's nothing else but konbini, so this stop decides what tonight and tomorrow taste like. Think crates of beer, fruity chu-hi, a bottle or two of local sake, crisps, and breakfast for Sunday and Monday.
how: Split the list: two people on drinks, two on snacks, two on breakfast, and two on ice and mixers.
Get enough for two nights. It closes at 18:00 and this is the only chance.
Taxis on to the villa take 6 minutes.
tips: Pick up a deck of cards or check whether the villa has board games. That's how Japanese groups do villa nights.
Pool the money on one card and split it later to keep the checkout fast.
wishes: w4: We love to drink
w10: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa – check in
stops.summary: Drop in, chill the drinks, and claim your rooms before heading straight back out.
stops.plan: Check in (from 15:00), put the drinks in the fridge and collect any forwarded bags.
stops.transport: Taxi (2 cars) to Hakone Glass no Mori, 6 min

guide.story: Your home for two nights is a private hot-spring villa in Sengokuhara, the misty, grassy high basin of Hakone. This is a quick stop, not a lounge. Get the cans in the fridge, grab any forwarded bags and settle the room fights now so nobody argues at midnight.
how: Check in (from 15:00) and find out how the villa's own hot spring works for later.
Load the fridge, and put the sake in last so it chills fastest.
Taxis to Glass no Mori take 6 minutes, so keep them waiting or pre-book.
tips: Ask about any quiet hours for the outdoor bath before your midnight soak.
Set out the bath towels now so nobody is hunting for them at night.
wishes: w11: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)

stops.name: Hakone Glass no Mori – Christmas crystal illumination
stops.nameJa: 箱根ガラスの森美術館 クリスタルイルミネーション
stops.summary: Venetian glass, crystal arches and a glass Christmas tree lighting up at dusk.
stops.plan: Arrive as dusk falls to see the crystal arches, the glass Christmas tree and the candles (lit 1–25 Dec) come on. Last entry is 17:00.
stops.transport: Walk 15 min west to Hakone Sushi

guide.story: Glass no Mori is a Venetian-glass museum set in a garden, and in December it turns into Hakone's best Christmas illumination. Crystal arches catch the last of the sunset, a towering glass tree glitters, and from 1–25 Dec there are candles as well. Arrive as the light fades and you watch the whole garden switch from gold to sparkle, which is perfect for group photos.
how: Arrive by 17:00 at the latest, which is last entry. The plan has you there at dusk.
Head straight for the crystal arches for the photos, then do the tree and the candles.
Walk 15 minutes west to dinner at Hakone Sushi.
tips: Buy the discounted pre-sale tickets online instead of paying ¥1,800 at the gate.
Keep your ticket stub, because same-day re-entry is allowed.
Hours can change in bad weather, so check the site that morning.
wishes: w8: We love to do it all
w10: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.name: Hakone Sushi
stops.summary: The sushi place in Sengokuhara, with a tatami room for 8 and a winter-only kinmedai shabu-shabu.
stops.plan: Early dinner in the booked tatami room: special-grade sushi, anago and the winter-only kinmedai shabu-shabu. Credit cards OK.
stops.transport: Pre-booked taxis (2 cars) down the mountain to Hakone-Yumoto, 24 min

guide.story: Hakone Sushi is where the locals go, a family counter-and-tatami place that's full most nights. Get the tatami room for all of you and order a spread of 特上寿司, anago sushi and the house はこねにぎり. The big winter move is 金目鯛のしゃぶしゃぶ: you swish slices of buttery golden-eye snapper through hot broth, which is exactly what a cold mountain night calls for. It's highly rated on Google and Tabelog, and cards are fine.
how: Phone 0460-84-7890 to book. They don't take reservations by DM or comment.
Order 特上寿司 (¥3,200), 穴子寿司 (¥2,600) or はこねにぎり (¥4,200). Prices exclude tax.
Share a few kinmedai shabu-shabu portions (¥2,700 each, excl. tax) around the table.
Leave at 18:30 in 2 pre-booked taxis. It's 24 minutes down to Yumoto, against 136 by train and bus.
tips: Book as soon as you can. Reviews say it's full even on weekdays.
Opening at 17:00 means you get the freshest start and an easy exit for the geisha show.
Pace the beer. Free-flowing drinks with the geisha are next.

w8: We love to do it all

stops.name: Hakone Yumoto Kenban – Furatto Geisha night
stops.nameJa: 箱根湯本見番「ふらっと芸者」／芸者カフェバーはな
stops.summary: Real Hakone geisha dance for you, then play ozashiki drinking games with them.
stops.plan: Doors open 19:30 for the 20:00 session (40 min). Three geisha dance, then you play ozashiki drinking games with them, drink included. Arrive early so all 8 sit together.
stops.transport: Pre-booked taxis (2 cars) back up to MONTA in Sengokuhara, 23 min

guide.story: Hakone-Yumoto is one of Japan's old geisha towns, and on the 3rd Saturday the Kenban opens its doors with Furatto Geisha. Three geisha perform a dance in kimono. Then the formality drops and they teach you ozashiki asobi, the rapid-fire party games where the loser drinks. It runs 40 minutes with a drink included, and it's the kind of night that becomes the trip's best story. Booking a geisha privately runs at an hourly rate, so this is a rare cheap way in.
how: Doors open 19:30 for the 20:00 session. Get there right at opening so all 8 sit together in the small hall.
It's walk-in, with no booking, so arrive early.
Ask for photos with the geisha when the games wind down.
Meet the 2 taxis for the 23-minute ride back up to MONTA.
tips: If the 20:00 slot looks rammed, the 18:30 session (entry from 18:00) is the fallback, though that means a faster dinner.
Throw yourselves into the games. The geisha love a loud, game group.
Events can change without notice, so check geisha.co.jp that day.
wishes: w3: If there are cool nightlife things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them
w4: We love to drink
w8: We love to do it all

stops.name: Ochanoma Shubo MONTA
stops.summary: Sengokuhara's one late-night izakaya-bar, and Saturday is your only night to hit it.
stops.plan: Saturday's second round: a long drinks list and home-style snacks. December bookings are capped at 2 hours; last entry 23:00. The shuttle takes max 7 and doesn't run late, so use taxis.
stops.transport: Taxi (2 cars) to the villa, 6 min

guide.story: MONTA feels like drinking in someone's cosy living room: home-style snacks, a long drinks list and a crowd that stays until midnight. It's highly rated, and reviewers mention groups of 8 booking ahead and using it as a second round, which is exactly your plan. It's closed Sunday and Monday, so tonight is the night.
how: Book online or by phone on 0460-83-9797 for 8. In December, seats are capped at 2 hours.
Arrive by taxi, since the shuttle takes max 7 and doesn't run 17:30-21:00 or after 23:00.
Last entry is 23:00, so you have plenty of margin. Leave at 23:30 for a 6-minute taxi to the villa.
tips: Pre-book the return taxis. Late at night in Sengokuhara, cars don't just appear.
It's completely non-smoking inside, and smokers step out to the area outside.
Order the homestyle snacks to soak up the evening before the villa round.

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa – onsen nightcap
stops.summary: End the night the Hakone way: cans in hand, in your own hot spring.
stops.plan: Drink the A Coop stock in the villa's own hot spring. This is the cheapest round of the night.

guide.story: Steam, stars and a chilled chu-hi in hot water: this is the moment the whole day was built for. The villa's own onsen means no closing time and no strangers, and the A Coop haul makes it the cheapest round of the night. Wind down, play cards and let the mountain quiet take over.
how: Pull the drinks from the fridge and take them to the bath.
Rotate in shifts if the tub can't fit all 8 at once.
Save some stock for tomorrow night.
tips: Alternate soaking with water. Hot springs plus a long night of drinking hit harder than you'd expect.
Keep the noise down outdoors out of respect for the neighbours.
wishes: w4: We love to drink
w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

days.title: First ropeway to steaming Owakudani · pirate ship · lakeside torii · Nobu wagyu lunch · sculpture park · craft beer · late burgers in Miyanoshita

notes.text: The Owakudani–Sounzan ropeway section is shut for maintenance today, with a replacement bus instead. Ride Togendai ⇄ Owakudani and back, and never head down the Sounzan side.
Fog or strong wind can stop the pirate ship, and volcanic gas readings can halt the ropeway. Check both before leaving the villa. Clear December mornings are your best shot at Fuji.

Funny's takes HotPepper requests only until 17:00 the day before, so it must be locked in by Saturday afternoon. Book Itoh Dining and Gora Brewery for 8 as well. Same-day bookings at either are phone only.
Savings today: the Freepass covers the ropeway, ship and buses, Nobu's lunch costs a fraction of dinner, and the museum's web ticket beats the gate price.
Evening buses back to Sengokuhara have stopped by the time you leave Funny's. Pre-book a pair of taxis home before you start drinking.

stops.name: Villa breakfast + morning soak
stops.summary: Coffee, A Coop leftovers and a fast hangover soak before Hakone's best morning.
stops.plan: Breakfast from the A Coop haul and a quick hangover soak, then out the door.
stops.transport: Hakone Tozan bus Sengokuhara → Togendai (Freepass), 9 min; take 2 taxis if the bus timing doesn't fit

guide.story: Last night's supermarket haul becomes breakfast: onigiri, yoghurt drinks and whatever survived the late snack raid. The private hot spring is the cure. Ten minutes in the water and the group is human again. Keep it moving, because the whole day hinges on being at Togendai when the first gondola swings out.
how: Eat between 07:30 and 08:25. Whoever is up first starts the kettle and fills the bath.
Pack day bags with Freepasses, phones charged, a warm layer and gloves. Owakudani is cold and windy.
Head out for the Tozan bus to Togendai. By car the run is 9 min, so if the bus timing doesn't fit, call a pair of taxis.
tips: Put the Freepasses in one person's pocket the night before so nobody is hunting for them at the door.
Taxi phrase: 'Togendai made onegaishimasu' (to Togendai, please).

stops.name: Hakone Ropeway Togendai ⇄ Owakudani + black eggs
stops.nameJa: 箱根ロープウェイ・大涌谷
stops.summary: First gondola over a steaming volcanic crater, with Fuji floating behind it if the sky plays nice.
stops.plan: First car at 09:00 (two sections, about 10 min each) while Fuji is clearest. Walk the sulphur vents, eat kuro-tamago black eggs, then ride back to Togendai. The Sounzan side is closed for maintenance, so don't go that way.
stops.transport: Walk 2 min to the Togendai pier

guide.story: From Togendai the ropeway climbs over forest, and then the ground simply opens up: yellow-white slopes hissing with sulphur vents and the rotten-egg smell hitting you before the car docks. Owakudani is the crater of an eruption from about 3,000 years ago and is still very much alive. That is also why gas readings can halt the line. On a clear December morning Fuji sits right over the ridge. Then there are the kuro-tamago, eggs boiled in the hot springs until the shells turn jet black. Legend says each one adds seven years to your life.
how: Be on the first car at 09:00. Each of the two sections is a 10 min ride, via Ubako.
At Owakudani, walk the vent viewpoints first while the light is clean, then queue for the black eggs.
Ride back the way you came to Togendai. The Sounzan section is closed, and its replacement bus gets stuck in traffic.
From the ropeway station it's a short walk down to the pirate ship pier.
tips: Black eggs are about ¥500 for a bag of 5, so buy one bag per pair. Peel them outside; the sulphur smell lingers.
Sit facing the downhill window on the ride up, and get the window on the other side on the way down, so everyone gets a Fuji shot.
If the line is suspended for gas, skip straight to the ship rather than waiting around.
guide.cost: Covered by the Freepass (fares from ¥780 without it); black eggs about ¥500 for 5
wishes: w5: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
w8: We love to do it all
w10: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.name: Lake Ashi pirate ship Togendai → Motohakone
stops.summary: A gaudy full-rigged pirate ship across Lake Ashi, with Fuji behind you.
stops.plan: Cross Lake Ashi on the deck with Fuji behind you. The ship calls at Hakone-machi and docks at Motohakone.
stops.address: 箱根町元箱根164桃源台港
stops.transport: Walk 5 min along the lake to Hakone Shrine

guide.story: It is completely ridiculous, a gilded galleon with cannons and carved figureheads, and it's brilliant. The crossing takes 25 minutes over cold, glassy water, with forested ridges on both sides and Fuji peeking over the northern shore. The ship calls at Hakone-machi and then glides into Motohakone, where the red torii comes into view from the water.
how: Board at Togendai pier on the 11:00 sailing window (11:00–11:40).
Go straight up to the open deck at the stern for the Fuji-behind-you shots, and stay out there even if it's cold.
Stay on past Hakone-machi and get off at Motohakone.
tips: The first-class deck upgrade is extra and not worth it for a crossing this short. The open deck has the better views.
On the approach to Motohakone, move to the side facing the shore so you see the lakeside torii from the water. Nobody else gets that angle.
Fog or strong wind can cancel sailings. Check at the pier before you commit.
guide.cost: Covered by the Freepass (first-class upgrade extra)
guide.hours: 09:30–16:40 today (one listing says later, so verify on the day)
wishes: w8: We love to do it all

stops.name: Hakone Shrine & Torii of Peace
stops.nameJa: 箱根神社 平和の鳥居
stops.summary: Cedar giants, mossy stone steps and Hakone's famous torii standing in the lake.
stops.plan: Walk the cedar-lined steps to the shrine and shoot the lakeside torii from the side path to skip the midday queue. The lakeside is slippery.
stops.transport: Hakone Tozan bus Motohakone-ko → Miyanoshita (Freepass), about 30 min, then Tozan train Miyanoshita → Gora, about 15 min

guide.story: A 5 min stroll along the shore from the pier brings you into a tunnel of enormous old cedars, with stone lanterns and steep moss-edged steps up to a vermilion shrine that has been here for over a thousand years. Below it, the Torii of Peace stands in the water of Lake Ashi. It is the shot everyone came for, and by midday the queue for the front-on photo can run 30 minutes or more. You don't need it: the side path gives you the gate with the lake and mountains behind, with no wait.
how: Climb the main cedar-lined steps to the shrine hall first. The grounds are free and open all day.
Walk down to the lakeside and shoot the torii from the side path instead of joining the queue.
If someone insists on the classic front-on shot, send one person to hold a place in the queue while the rest explore.
Wrap up by 12:40 and head for Gora. By road it's 19 min; the Freepass bus-and-train route takes longer.
tips: The stones by the water are slippery, so have sneakers on, not party shoes.
The shrine office sells omamori (lucky charms) and goshuin (stamped shrine seals) 8:15-17:00. A charm makes a cheap, light souvenir.
The treasure hall costs ¥500 and can be skipped on a day this packed.
guide.hours: Grounds open 24 hours; treasure hall 09:00–16:30, last entry 16:00
wishes: w8: We love to do it all

facts.text: Last entry 16:00

Amulet and goshuin sales are open 8:15-17:00 at the shrine office.

stops.name: Itoh Dining by Nobu – teppan lunch
stops.nameJa: 伊藤ダイニング by NOBU
stops.summary: Nobu-team wagyu seared on the teppan in front of you, at lunch prices.
stops.plan: Wagyu teppanyaki cooked in front of you at lunch prices: Select Lunch from ¥3,000 + tax, far less than dinner. Booked for 8; the counter may split you 4+4.
stops.transport: Walk 16 min downhill to the museum

guide.story: This is the splurge, done the smart way. Itoh Dining is the Nobu team's Hakone teppanyaki room, where a chef works the hot plate a foot from your face, searing wagyu and garlic until the counter smells incredible. It's highly rated on Google and the place to treat yourselves, but dinner here is a different price bracket. The Select Lunch starts at ¥3,000 plus tax, so eight people eat Nobu-level beef for the price of an izakaya night.
how: Arrive for your 13:45 booking. The counter may seat you as two groups of four, which works well because each side gets its own chef show.
Base level is the Select Lunch (about ¥3,300 with tax). Anyone going big can upgrade to a wagyu set at roughly ¥8,000–15,000.
Finish by 14:40, then walk 16 min downhill to the Open-Air Museum.
tips: Same-day bookings are phone only. If your plans slip, call rather than just turning up.
Agree as a group beforehand whether you're going base set or wagyu, so the bill doesn't turn into a debate.
Go easy on lunch drinks. The brewery is next.
guide.cost: Select Lunch ¥3,000 + tax (~¥3,300 pp); wagyu sets ~¥8,000–15,000 pp
guide.booking: Booked for 8. Phone or online; same-day by phone only
wishes: w10: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
stops.price: ¥1,800 pp web ticket (¥2,000 at the gate)
stops.summary: Giant sculptures on misty hillsides, a stained-glass tower to climb and a hot footbath to finish.
stops.plan: The grounds go quiet after 15:30. See the giant outdoor sculptures, climb the Symphonic Sculpture stained-glass tower, visit the Picasso pavilion and finish at the footbath. Last entry 16:30.
stops.transport: Walk 16 min back up towards Gora Station

guide.story: Huge bronze figures lounge on the lawns with mountains behind them, there's a giant head lying on its side, and the Symphonic Sculpture is a tower whose inside is wrapped floor to ceiling in stained glass. Climb the spiral and the late-winter light turns everything jewel-coloured. The Picasso pavilion holds a surprisingly deep collection. The grounds are big enough that it never feels crowded, and after 15:30 they go properly quiet.
how: Buy web tickets before you arrive: ¥1,800 instead of ¥2,000 at the window, and you skip the line.
Head for the Symphonic Sculpture first and climb it, then the Picasso pavilion.
Save the footbath for last. Shoes off, feet in the hot water, ten minutes of bliss.
Leave by 16:20 and walk 16 min back up towards Gora for beers.
tips: Last entry is 16:30, but you're arriving at 15:00, so you're fine. Just don't dawdle at lunch.
Sculpture photos are allowed for personal use, so post away.
Groups of 15 or more need a group booking. At 8 you just buy individual web tickets.

guide.booking: Buy WEB tickets online in advance

stops.name: Gora Brewery & Grill
stops.summary: House-brewed craft beer and wood-fired grill plates as the mountains go dark.
stops.plan: House craft beers and wood-fired grill plates at a booked big table as the sun goes down. Closes at 20:30.
stops.transport: Taxi (2 cars) Gora → Miyanoshita, 6 min

guide.story: The best craft beer in Hakone is brewed right here, and it pours fresh at a big table that fits all eight of you. You arrive straight from the museum with cold cheeks, and the room is warm and loud and smells of woodsmoke from the grill. Order a flight to work out your favourite, then commit to pints. Keep the food to sharing plates, because there's a second dinner coming.
how: Arrive for your booked table at 16:35. There's a ¥500 per person table charge.
Start with a tasting flight around the table, then order rounds of whatever won.
Get a few grill plates to share, not full mains. Burgers are next.
Leave at 18:50. Two taxis to Miyanoshita take 6 min. The Tozan train (Gora 19:00 → Miyanoshita 19:12, ¥160) is the budget option but is 29 min door to door.
tips: Same-day table changes are phone only, so call if you're running late from the museum.
Taxis are the smarter move here. You'll walk into Funny's on time instead of rushing.
Budget about ¥4,000–6,000 each with beers. Good value for the best taps in town.

stops.name: American Diner & Bar Funny's
stops.nameJa: アメリカンダイナー&バー ファニーズ
stops.summary: Hakone's rare late-night spot: big American burgers and drinks until near midnight.
stops.plan: Sunday dinner and drinks at Hakone's late spot, booked via HotPepper. Order the LA burger (¥1,870) and loco moco (¥1,650) and keep the drinks coming.
stops.transport: Pre-booked taxis (2 cars) Miyanoshita → Sengokuhara villa, 14 min (the evening buses have stopped)

guide.story: Hakone goes to bed early. Funny's doesn't. It's a small American diner-bar in Miyanoshita with neon, loud music and burgers that recent reviewers call some of the best in Japan, and it's open until 24:00 when nearly everything else is dark. It's a tight room, so eight of you basically take it over, and the friendly staff seem to enjoy that. This is your Sunday night out in the mountains.
how: Walk in at 19:00 on your HotPepper booking.
Order the LA burger (¥1,870) and the loco moco (¥1,650), a Hawaiian plate of rice, burger patty, fried egg and gravy, to share around. Then get the drinks flowing.
Stay until 22:45, then into the pre-booked taxis. It's 14 min back to the villa in Sengokuhara.
tips: HotPepper requests close at 17:00 the day before, so this had to be done by Saturday. A seat-only booking adds ¥300 per person.
If the room can't fit eight together, split into two tables side by side. It's still one party.
Book the return taxis when you sit down, not at closing time. Taxis are scarce in Miyanoshita late at night.
It's closed on Monday, so tonight is your only shot.
guide.cost: ~¥3,000–4,000 pp; LA burger ¥1,870, loco moco ¥1,650, soft drinks ¥400

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa – last onsen night
stops.summary: The last soak under the cold mountain sky, drink in hand.
stops.plan: Finish the drinks in the hot spring, then pack for an early checkout.

guide.story: Back at the villa, the steam rises off the bath into the freezing December air, and that alone is worth the trip to Hakone. Ease in with a final can from the fridge and replay the day: the crater, the pirate ship, the wagyu. It's your last night with your own hot spring, so make it count, but keep it gentle.
how: Get straight into the bath when the taxis drop you off at 23:10.
Pack before the second drink, not after. Checkout is early tomorrow.
Lights out by 01:00.
tips: Drink plenty of water between beers. Hot water and alcohol dehydrate you fast, so keep soaks short and take breaks.
Set two alarms for the morning and put one person in charge of the final sweep for chargers.

notes.text: Passports on you all day: the outlet tax refund is done store by store and needs the physical passport, not a photo.
Download the Shopping Navi app before you leave the villa. The outlet coupons are free and need no membership.
Book the Mishima → Shin-Osaka seats together on smartEX this morning, so all 8 of you sit in one block with room for the outlet haul.
Big transit day: villa, outlets, lights, shinkansen, Osaka. Bags ride in the taxis, so keep shopping bags consolidated and carry only what you need at Tokinosumika.
Round1 runs past the last trains. Plan on two taxis home to Kujō and keep a little cash spare.

[BRING] Passports on you all day: from 1 Nov 2026 Japan's tax-free system is refund-based, so you pay tax-inclusive prices at the till and claim the refund electronically via customs when you leave Japan. Stores may still scan your physical passport.

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa – soak, pack, check out
stops.summary: One last steaming soak in Sengokuhara before the day turns into a sprint.
stops.plan: Breakfast and a last soak, then out by the fixed 10:00 checkout.
stops.transport: 2 pre-booked taxis with luggage to Gotemba Premium Outlets, 25 min (the direct Tozan bus from Sengoku, ~¥1,120 pp, works if you travel light)

guide.story: This is the slow hour before a very fast day. Get up early enough for breakfast and one more soak, with the mountain air cold on your shoulders and the water hot. Sengokuhara is quiet on a Monday morning in December, and it will be the calmest you feel until tomorrow. Checkout is fixed, so treat the soak as the reward for packing first.
how: Pack everything before breakfast and line the bags up by the door, so the last soak is not rushed.
Take breakfast and then the bath, and be dressed with bags out before the 10:00 checkout.
Load both pre-booked taxis. The ride to Gotemba Premium Outlets is 25 min by car.
tips: If anyone is travelling light, the direct Tozan bus from Sengoku (~¥1,120 pp) also works. With 8 people's luggage, though, the taxis win.
Leave one empty duffel or foldable bag at the top of a suitcase. You will need it by lunchtime.

stops.name: Gotemba Premium Outlets
stops.nameJa: 御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット
stops.summary: Around 290 stores, Fuji on the horizon, and a Monday crowd small enough to actually shop.
stops.plan: Monday is quiet. Split up across about 290 stores (Nike, New Balance, Beams, United Arrows, Coach) with Shopping Navi app coupons, and meet at the food court around 12:30 for lunch. Bring passports; keep receipts and goods unopened for the tax refund.
stops.transport: Hakone Tozan bus Outlet–Tokinosumika line, 18 min (or taxis with luggage)

guide.story: Gotemba is Japan's heavyweight outlet, with around 290 stores spread across open-air streets and Mt Fuji looming over the car park on a clear day. The roster is what you came for: Nike, Adidas, New Balance, Beams, United Arrows and Coach. A Monday in December means short fitting-room lines instead of the weekend crush. Since 1 Nov 2026 tax-free shopping works on a refund basis: you pay the tax-inclusive price at the till and the consumption tax is refunded after you leave Japan, so prices do not drop at the till.
how: Arrive near the 10:00 opening and split into pairs or small crews by interest, for example sneakers, Japanese streetwear or bags.
Open the Shopping Navi app at each store and check for coupons before you pay.
Regroup at the food court at 12:30 for lunch (~¥1,500 pp), compare hauls, then go back out for round two.
Be at the taxi rank by 15:45. Tokinosumika is 18 min by taxi.
tips: Under the refund system from 1 Nov 2026 goods are no longer sealed at purchase. Keep your receipts and the goods together, and complete the refund process with customs before you leave Japan.
Ask staff "Menzei dekimasu ka?" (Can I get tax-free?) before you queue at the till.
Set up a group chat pin for the food court meeting spot. The site is big and easy to drift across.
guide.booking: Download the Shopping Navi app for coupons (no membership)

stops.name: Gotemba Kogen Tokinosumika winter illumination + beer hall
stops.nameJa: 時之栖イルミネーション
stops.price: Lights free/low cost; beer ~¥700+, dinner ~¥3,000 pp
stops.summary: Walk a tunnel of light at dusk, then take over a long table in a brewery beer hall.
stops.plan: Walk the light tunnel and watch the fountain light show as it gets dark, then dinner and Gotemba Kogen Beer in the big beer hall.
stops.transport: 2 taxis to Mishima Station, 28 min

guide.story: Tokinosumika's winter illumination is one of the region's biggest: a long tunnel of lights and a fountain that runs a choreographed light show once darkness falls. Arrive while there is still some sky colour, around dusk (~16:30), and you get to watch the whole place switch on. Then move into the beer hall, a big, loud room made for groups. Gotemba Kogen Beer is brewed right on site, so the first round tastes like it came from metres away, because it did.
how: Do the light tunnel first while it is fresh dark, for photos, and catch the fountain show.
Head into the beer hall and grab one long table for all 8 of you.
Order the house Gotemba Kogen Beer flights or pints (~¥700+), with dinner around ¥3,000 pp.
Leave by 18:15. Mishima Station is 28 min by taxi.
tips: Start with the lights, not the beer. Once you sit down in the hall, nobody gets back up.
Dress warm. It is properly cold up here after dark in December.
Line up the two taxis to Mishima before the last round, so you are not stranded for the shinkansen.
guide.cost: Illumination free/low cost; beer ~¥700+, dinner ~¥3,000 pp

stops.summary: A bullet-train glide west from Fuji country to Osaka, seats together and bags stowed.
stops.plan: Take a Hikari if one fits; otherwise Kodama to Nagoya and change to a Nozomi. Reserve seats together on smartEX.

guide.story: This is your reset: two-plus hours of padded seats while Shizuoka and Nagoya flash past in the dark. A Hikari from Mishima is the cleanest option. If the timing does not work, a Kodama to Nagoya with a hop onto a Nozomi gets you there just as well. Grab konbini snacks or a can at the station and let the outlet legs recover.
how: Book seats together on smartEX in advance. Pick a Hikari if one fits, otherwise Kodama to Nagoya and a change to a Nozomi.
Use the oversized-luggage area or the space behind the last row for the bigger bags and shopping hauls.
At Shin-Osaka, follow signs to the Midosuji line. The metro leaves 21:21 to Hommachi, then the Chuo line 21:38 to Kujo (¥290).
tips: The connection at Shin-Osaka is tight. Have IC cards topped up so nobody gets stuck at a fare machine.
If you miss the metro or the bags feel too heavy, a taxi to Kujo is 15 min.

stops.name: Dotonbori / Namba – first Osaka night
stops.summary: Your first Osaka night: canal neon, giant signs and standing bars that pour fast.
stops.plan: First Osaka night: walk the neon canal and drink at standing bars and izakaya. The Osaka research leg has the specific bar list.
stops.transport: Walk 8 min to Sennichimae

guide.story: Dotonbori is Osaka at full volume. Mechanical crabs and blazing billboards hang over the canal, and street food smoke drifts off the takoyaki stalls while bridges fill with people taking the obligatory Glico-sign photo. Osaka drinks differently from Tokyo. It is looser, louder and cheaper, with standing bars where you elbow in, order a highball and end up talking to the table next to you. Treat tonight as the taster. The Osaka research leg has the deeper bar list for later nights.
how: Come up from Namba and walk the canal along Ebisubashi for the neon first.
Hop between standing bars and izakaya. Order highballs or nama biru with takoyaki and kushikatsu as you go.
Budget around ¥4,000 pp, then start drifting toward Sennichimae just after midnight. Round1 is a walk of 8 min.
tips: At kushikatsu places the rule is no double-dipping in the shared sauce.
With 8 people, split into two groups of four. Small standing bars fit four far more easily than eight.
Say "Kanpai!" loud. Osaka bartenders appreciate the energy.
wishes: Ending the night/nightlife in Osaka
We love to drink
We love to do it all

stops.name: Round1 Stadium Sennichimae (Namba)
stops.summary: Round1 after midnight: karaoke, bowling and arcade chaos to close day three.
stops.plan: Late-night Round1: karaoke, bowling and the arcade. There are no go-karts here. Check the same-day closing time.
stops.transport: Taxi (2 cars) back to Kujō House, about 10 min

guide.story: Round1 Stadium Sennichimae is the after-hours playground you asked for. It has bowling lanes, a sprawling arcade full of rhythm games and crane machines, and karaoke rooms where 8 people can scream their way to the small hours. There are no go-karts here, just pure game-centre energy right on the edge of Namba's nightlife.
how: Check the same-day closing time at the counter or on the Round1 site before you commit to packages.
Start with a bowling game while everyone is still steady, then move into a karaoke room for the rest of the night.
Budget around ¥2,000–3,000 pp, and finish with two taxis back to Kujō House.
tips: Karaoke rooms are the best value per head for a group of 8. Ask about a free-time (furii taimu) plan.
Have the Japanese address of Kujō House ready on a phone for the drivers.

todos.text: Book 8 Romancecar seats together, Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto, 19 Dec morning
todos.detail: Seats open 1 month ahead and a December Saturday sells out. The seat is a separate ticket from the Freepass.

todos.text: Buy 8 × 3-day Hakone Freepass (from Shinjuku, ¥7,500) on Odakyu EMot
todos.detail: On sale from 1 month before the ride date. Ticket machines sell same-day passes only. Buying digitally skips the Shinjuku counter queue.

todos.text: Reserve 2 large private open-air rooms at Hakone Yuryo, 19 Dec 10:00–12:00
todos.detail: Bookable from 1 month before until 15:00 the day before. Weekend rate is ¥10,400 per room.

todos.text: Reserve Hakone Sushi tatami room for 8, Sat 19 Dec 17:00 (phone 0460-84-7890)
todos.detail: Phone bookings only (no DMs). Reviews say it's full even on weekdays.

todos.text: Book Itoh Dining by Nobu lunch for 8, Sun 20 Dec 13:45
todos.detail: Book 2–4 weeks ahead online or by phone. Accept a 4+4 split at the counter if needed.

todos.text: Book Shinkansen Mishima → Shin-Osaka, 21 Dec ~19:00, 8 seats together
todos.detail: Use smartEX and check the EX early-booking (Hayatoku) fares, which need booking several days ahead.

todos.text: Reserve MONTA for 8, Sat 19 Dec 21:30 (phone 0460-83-9797 or online)
todos.detail: December seats are limited to 2 hours and last entry is 23:00. The shuttle carries max 7 and isn't available late, so take taxis.

todos.text: Book Gora Brewery & Grill table for 8, Sun 20 Dec 16:30
todos.detail: Walk-ins may be turned away when busy. ¥500 pp table charge.

todos.text: Book Funny's for 8 via HotPepper, Sun 20 Dec 19:00
todos.detail: The room is small, so book early. Hard deadline is 17:00 the day before.

todos.text: Book taxis: Sat 19 Dec 14:30 Yumoto → A Coop Sengokuhara, 18:40 Hakone Sushi → Yumoto, 20:50 Yumoto → MONTA; Sun 20 Dec 22:45 Funny's → villa; Mon 21 Dec 10:00 villa → Gotemba Outlets
todos.detail: Hakone has few taxis at night, and the Sengokuhara buses stop early and are slow from Yumoto. You need 2 cars (or jumbo taxis) each time.

todos.text: Check luggage plan: villa early drop or Hakone Carry Service on 19 Dec; storage at Gotemba Outlets/Tokinosumika on 21 Dec; or takkyubin straight to Kujō House
todos.detail: Confirm whether the villa accepts deliveries and whether Kujō House can receive bags sent from Tokyo.

todos.text: Check Tokinosumika illumination start time and the bus/taxi link to Mishima Station
todos.detail: Opening hours and the Mishima link weren't verified.

todos.text: Buy Hakone Glass no Mori online pre-sale tickets and Open-Air Museum web tickets (¥1,800)
todos.detail: Online tickets are discounted and skip the window.

todos.text: Check Furatto Geisha is still on for Sat 19 Dec (20:00 session), and check the pirate ship and ropeway winter timetables
todos.detail: The geisha event can change without notice. Ship hours conflict between sources (16:40 vs 18:00), and ropeway service depends on volcanic gas levels.

todos.text: Check the new tax-free refund rules; bring passports to the outlets
todos.detail: From what we know (unconfirmed), the refund system starts 1 Nov 2026: you pay tax in the shop and claim it back at the airport. Keep receipts and don't open goods.

budget.note: Covers Shinjuku→Hakone plus trains, ropeway, pirate ship and Tozan buses. The ropeway and ship loop alone use up much of its value.

coverage.wish: Osaka base, but during the day we will commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed
coverage.how: The Hakone leg hands over to the Osaka base on 21 Dec: Mishima → Shin-Osaka shinkansen, then check in at Kujō House (Nishi-ku) at 21:50. Kyoto and Nara day commutes belong to the Osaka leg, which this Hakone research doesn't cover.
The first Osaka night (21 Dec) ends in Namba with Dotonbori and Round1, then a taxi to Kujō House. The Hakone nights end at the villa's hot spring.

coverage.wish: If there are cool nightlife things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them
coverage.how: Nightlife in the neighbouring areas: the Furatto Geisha drinking-game night in Yumoto (19 Dec), MONTA (19 Dec), Gora Brewery and Funny's (20 Dec), and the Tokinosumika beer hall (21 Dec).
Drinking every day: beer at Yuryo, the geisha drink, MONTA, onsen nightcaps, a brewpub, Funny's, the Gotemba beer hall and Dotonbori.

coverage.wish: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
coverage.how: A 07:30 Romancecar, the first 09:00 ropeway car, and late nights every day (01:30, 01:00, 02:30). Taxis replace the slow bus up from Yumoto. Monday's checkout runs straight into outlets, lights and a night train to Osaka with no dead time.
Hakone and Odawara have no Round1, so it's on the night of 21 Dec at Round1 Stadium Sennichimae in Namba. Add more Round1 sessions in the Osaka and Tokyo legs.
The Yumoto souvenir street (19 Dec) and a full weekday at Gotemba Premium Outlets (21 Dec, 10:30–15:45).

coverage.wish: We love to do it all
coverage.how: A private onsen, geisha, illuminations, the volcano ropeway, the pirate ship, the shrine torii, a sculpture museum, wagyu, sushi, craft beer, outlets and Round1, all in 3 days.
No go-kart activities anywhere in the plan.

coverage.wish: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes
coverage.how: Savings: the 3-day Freepass (¥7,500 instead of separate fares), Nobu at lunch instead of dinner, online tickets for Glass no Mori and the Open-Air Museum, supermarket drinks for the villa nights, outlet app coupons, the tax refund with passports, and smartEX early shinkansen fares. Booking dates are in the todos.

coverage.wish: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)
coverage.how: Leave Ninja House (Toshima) on the morning of 19 Dec, stay at Hot Spring Hakone Villa 19–21 Dec (in 15:00, out 10:00), and check in at Kujō House (Osaka) on the night of 21 Dec. Garfield House (Shinjuku) belongs to the final Tokyo leg before the 29 Dec Haneda flight, outside this leg.
